history_summary.value: Bred in the 1970s at the University of Ljubljana's Biotechnical Faculty from imported Rhode Island Red stock, the Slovenian Brown became a popular layer on both large and small farms. It is now kept mainly at the university's poultry research center and used as a parent for the Prelux commercial crossbreeds.

Developed at the University of Ljubljana's Biotechnical Faculty and consolidated as a breed by 1968, the Slovenian Silver was selected for a sex-linked white plumage gene useful in crossbreeding. It is kept mainly at the university's poultry research center and used as a parent for the Prelux commercial crossbreeds.

history_summary.value: The Sombor Kaporka was created in the early 1900s in the Vojvodina region of northern Serbia by crossing imported Sulmtaler and Houdan chickens with local birds. A breed standard for it was set around 1918, and it is raised today as a dual-purpose egg and meat bird.

history_summary.value: The Speckledy (also sold as Speckled Ranger) is a modern UK hybrid from a Rhode Island Red x Marans cross, bred as a heavy, hardy layer of speckled chestnut-brown eggs.

The Stara Zagora Red was created around 1970 by crossing local hens from the Stara Zagora region of Bulgaria with Rhode Island Red cocks, with the red colour fixed by the second generation. It is now a rare breed, kept mainly by the Bulgarian Poultry Institute and a handful of breeders.

history_summary.value: The Starlight Green Egger is a modern hatchery hybrid marketed as a dependable green-egg layer, produced the same way other 'egger' hybrids are: crossing blue-egg and brown-egg laying lines rather than breeding to a fixed standard.

The Sulmtaler descends from country chickens of the Styrian valleys of southern Austria, which were crossed with Cochin, Dorking and Houdan stock in the late 1800s to make heavier fattening birds. Around 1900 breeders gathered the remaining original-type stock and re-established the breed, which then spread to Germany, the Netherlands and England.

history_summary.value: According to legend the Sultan was kept as an ornamental bird in the palace gardens of the Ottoman sultans in Turkey, and all Western stock descends from birds sent to a London poultry editor in 1854. history_summary.value: The Sumatra descends from fighting cocks brought from the Indonesian island of Sumatra to the United States in 1847, and later to Germany and Britain. history_summary.value: One of Britain's oldest chicken breeds, the Sussex was shown as early as 1845 and given a formal breed standard in 1902, after which it and the Rhode Island Red became the two leading British meat breeds until commercial hybrids took over. A breed club revived it after near-extinction in the early 1900s, and it is now raised as a calm, cold-hardy dual-purpose bird suitable for beginners.

history_summary.value: The Valdarnese is a white Italian breed from the upper Arno valley in Tuscany, first described in 1899 and nearly wiped out in the 20th century by intensive farming and competition from the White Leghorn. history_summary.value: Vanaraja is a dual-purpose backyard chicken developed by ICAR's Directorate of Poultry Research in Hyderabad for rural households that scavenge-feed their birds. It grows fast, resists disease, and is now distributed across many Indian states from the Hyderabad center.

history_summary.value: The Welsummer was bred in the early 1900s in the Dutch village of Welsum from a mix of Rhode Island Red, Barnevelder, Partridge Leghorn, Cochin and Wyandotte stock, and reached a fixed standard by 1922-23.
